business_problem: Gilbert + Tobin needed to improve research, drafting, analysis, and operational workflows across a law firm without compromising client confidentiality, governance requirements, or human accountability.
solution_summary: Gilbert + Tobin started with ChatGPT Enterprise in operations teams, then expanded into marketing, business development, recruitment, finance, technology, and legal use cases once governance was in place. The rollout combined CEO-led sponsorship, enablement, approved-task guidance, data-processing controls, and Australian data residency so employees could use AI within the firm's confidentiality requirements. Teams now use ChatGPT for pitch synthesis, recruitment research, data extraction, analysis, deep research, documentation, and pressure testing via a custom GPT built from approved CEO materials. Codex extends the same model from assistance into execution, helping produce audit reports across 300 entities, validate file sets, build a Python application from specifications, and accelerate selected conflict, KYC, AML, and related checks before human review. This lets the firm standardize operational intelligence while preserving professional judgment over every final deliverable.

data_flow: Employees submit research, drafting, compliance, and operational tasks into ChatGPT Enterprise or Codex within governed access controls. Outputs can pull from approved organizational context or specifications, then move through human review and sign-off before they affect client or business processes.
business_outcome: Gilbert + Tobin more than doubled typical tool adoption, compressed operational workflows from hours to minutes, avoided large batches of manual work, and created a governance-first template for AI adoption inside a law firm.
